domain:
    # Dimensions for Cholesky factorization
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)      # reduction index for Cholesky inner products

    # Dimensions for SPD (symmetric positive-definite) matrix construction
    p: dim in [0, N)      # row index for SPD build
    q: dim in [0, N)      # column index for SPD build
    t: dim in [0, N)      # reduction index for SPD inner products

data:
    # Single global matrix, as in the original code: 
    # - after initialization it holds an SPD matrix,
    # - after factorization its lower triangle holds the Cholesky factor L.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major, full N x N

    # Temporary SPD matrix used during initialization (matches B in the C code).
    B[p, q]: temporary DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * N + q   # row-major, full N x N

parameters:
    N: int                        # problem size (matrix dimension)
    TI: int                       # tile size for i in Cholesky (sequential, cache tuning)
    TJ: int                       # tile size for j in Cholesky and SPD (cache tuning)
    TT: int                       # tile size for t in SPD construction (cache tuning)
    V:  int                       # vector width for inner products over k and t

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Build initial lower-triangular matrix in A, with unit diagonal.
    #    This matches the Polybench init_array() logic.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    build_lower:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, N):
                if j <= i:
                    # A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
                    A[i, j] = ((- (j mod N)) / N) + 1
                else:
                    # A[i][j] = 0;
                    A[i, j] = 0
            # A[i][i] = 1;  (override to ensure exact 1 on the diagonal)
            A[i, i] = 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Form a symmetric positive-definite matrix B = A * A^T.
    #    This matches the B[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t] loop nest.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    make_spd:
        for p in [0, N), q in [0, N):
            B[p, q] = sum(t in [0, N), A[p, t] * A[q, t])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Copy SPD matrix B back into A.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    copy_spd:
        for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
            A[i, j] = B[i, j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. In-place Cholesky factorization of A.
    #    After this, A’s lower triangle equals L such that:
    #        (SPD input from step 3) = L * L^T.
    #
    #    This is a direct translation of the Polybench code:
    #       for (i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    #         for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #           for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
    #           A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #         }
    #         for (k = 0; k < i; k++) A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
    #         A[i][i] = sqrt(A[i][i]);
    #       }
    #
    #    We express the inner loops as explicit reductions.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    cholesky_offdiag:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, N):
                if j < i:
                    # A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]) / A[j,j]
                    A[i, j] = ( A[i, j]
                                - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) / A[j, j]

    cholesky_diag:
        for i in [0, N):
            # A[i,i] = sqrt(A[i,i] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k]^2)
            A[i, i] = sqrt( A[i, i]
                            - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

optimization:
    # ==============================================================
    # Optimizations for SPD construction: B[p,q] = sum_t A[p,t] * A[q,t]
    # ==============================================================
    # Treat make_spd as a GEMM-like kernel over (p, q, t).

    # Tile rows and columns for better cache locality.
    block(p, P, TI)      # P indexes tiles of SPD rows
    block(q, Q, TJ)      # Q indexes tiles of SPD columns

    # Tile the reduction dimension t to improve L1/L2 reuse of A rows.
    block(t, T, TT)

    # Parallelize across row/column tiles: outer tiles are independent.
    parallelize(P)       # distribute row tiles of SPD across cores
    parallelize(Q)       # (optionally) further parallelize column tiles

    # Vectorize over the reduction dimension, which is contiguous in memory.
    vectorize(T, V)      # compute V-way FMA along t within each partial sum
    # (Equivalently: vectorize(t, V) inside the innermost loop of the SPD kernel.)

    # ==============================================================
    # Optimizations for Cholesky factorization.
    # ==============================================================
    # NOTE: The Cholesky algorithm has strong data dependencies:
    #   - Rows must be processed in increasing i (each row i depends
    #     on all previous rows 0..i-1 via A[j,j] and A[j,k]).
    #   - For a fixed i, columns j < i must be processed in increasing j
    #     because A[i,j] depends on A[i,k] for all k < j.
    #
    # Therefore we do NOT parallelize over i or j, but we still exploit
    # cache locality and inner-product vectorization.

    # Block i and j into panels/tiles to improve cache locality.
    # The triangular condition (j < i) is still enforced inside the tiles.
    block(i, I, TI)      # panel blocking over rows; I is outer panel index
    block(j, J, TJ)      # blocking over columns within each row

    # Keep I sequential due to row dependencies; do not parallelize(I).

    # Vectorize the inner-product reductions in k: A[i,j] -= sum_k A[i,k]*A[j,k]
    # and A[i,i] -= sum_k A[i,k]^2. A’s rows are stored contiguously, so
    # A[i,k] and A[j,k] are both nicely vectorizable along k.
    vectorize(k, V)

    # Unroll the j-loop inside each row i to expose instruction-level
    # parallelism when the active j-range is small (near the diagonal).
    unroll(j, 4)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # Optional higher-level tuning suggestions (kept as comments)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The sequential nature of the i- and j-loops prevents coarse-grain
    #   parallelization of the Cholesky phase. For very large N, a
    #   blocked Cholesky algorithm could be modeled by:
    #       * factoring diagonal blocks (I panels) with this unblocked
    #         kernel (sequential),
    #       * updating the trailing matrix with GEMM-like tiles (which
    #         can then use the same SPD tiling/parallelization strategy
    #         as above).
    #   That refactoring would introduce additional temporary tiles but
    #   can remain within the 1.5x memory overhead limit.
    #
    # - If tiny floating-point differences are acceptable, one can add
    #   a temporary array inv_diag[j] to cache 1 / A[j,j] after each
    #   diagonal update, and then replace division in the off-diagonal
    #   update with multiplication by inv_diag[j]. This reduces the
    #   number of expensive divides at the cost of an extra N-sized
    #   temporary.

```text
domain:
    # Problem size (from cholesky.hpp)
    n: dim in [0, N)

    # Global row/column indices
    i: dim in [0, n)
    j: dim in [0, n)

    # Inner-product indices
    k: dim in [0, n)

    # Indices used during SPD (A * Aᵀ) construction
    r: dim in [0, n)
    s: dim in [0, n)
    t: dim in [0, n)

data:
    # A holds:
    #   - after Stage 1: lower-triangular L₀
    #   - after Stage 2: SPD matrix A = L₀ L₀ᵀ
    #   - after Stage 3: in-place Cholesky factor L such that A ≈ L Lᵀ
    #
    # We model A in row-major layout: A[i, j] ≡ A[i][j] in the C code.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * n + j       # row-major

    # Temporary matrix used only while forming A * Aᵀ.
    B[r, s]: temp DATA_TYPE = (r, s) -> r * n + s        # row-major

parameters:
    n: int   # matrix order (N from cholesky.hpp)

computation:
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 1: initialize a unit-diagonal lower-triangular matrix L₀ in A
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C reference:
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
    #       A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
    #     for (j = i+1; j < n; j++)
    #       A[i][j] = 0;
    #     A[i][i] = 1;
    #   }
    #
    # Note: for 0 ≤ j < n, (-j % n) is in {0, -1, ..., -(n-1)}, so the
    # value is 1 - (j / n) in floating point.
    L0_init:
      for i in [0, n), j in [0, n):
          if j <= i:
              A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)(- (j mod n)) / (DATA_TYPE)n + (DATA_TYPE)1
          else:
              A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

      # Explicitly set diagonal to 1, as in the original init_array.
      for i in [0, n):
          A[i, i] = (DATA_TYPE)1

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 2: make A symmetric positive semi-definite via A ← A * Aᵀ
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Conceptual C code:
    #   for (r = 0; r < n; r++)
    #     for (s = 0; s < n; s++) {
    #       B[r][s] = 0;
    #       for (t = 0; t < n; t++)
    #         B[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    #     }
    #   for (r = 0; r < n; r++)
    #     for (s = 0; s < n; s++)
    #       A[r][s] = B[r][s];
    SPD_build:
      for r in [0, n), s in [0, n):
          B[r, s] = (DATA_TYPE)0
          for t in [0, n):
              B[r, s] += A[r, t] * A[s, t]

      SPD_copy_back:
        for r in [0, n), s in [0, n):
            A[r, s] = B[r, s]

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 3: in-place Cholesky factorization A = L Lᵀ (lower L in A)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Original Polybench kernel (with A[i][j] row-major):
    #
    #   for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    #     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
    #       for (k = 0; k < j; k++)
    #         A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
    #       A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    #     }
    #     for (k = 0; k < i; k++)
    #       A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
    #     A[i][i] = sqrt(A[i][i]);
    #   }
    #
    # We make the accumulation explicit in temporaries to reduce redundant
    # memory traffic but keep the same mathematical operation.
    Cholesky_factor:
      for i in seq([0, n)):               # must be strictly sequential
          # Off-diagonal elements in row i: j = 0 .. i-1
          for j in seq([0, i)):           # also sequential due to data deps
              acc_ij = (DATA_TYPE)0
              for k in [0, j):            # pure dot product over k
                  acc_ij += A[i, k] * A[j, k]
              A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - acc_ij) / A[j, j]

          # Diagonal element A[i, i]
          acc_ii = (DATA_TYPE)0
          for k in [0, i):
              acc_ii += A[i, k] * A[i, k]
          A[i, i] = (DATA_TYPE)sqrt( (double)(A[i, i] - acc_ii) )

optimization:
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Keep both A and B in row-major form:
    #   - accesses A[r, t] / A[s, t] in SPD_build are contiguous in t
    #   - accesses A[i, k] / A[j, k] in Cholesky_factor are contiguous in k
    # This matches the original Buffer layout (first index contiguous).

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 2 (SPD_build): dense symmetric matrix–matrix multiply A * Aᵀ
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Treat SPD_build as a GEMM-style kernel over (r, s, t) with independent
    # (r, s) results and a reduction in t:
    #
    #   B[r, s] = sum_{t=0..n-1} A[r, t] * A[s, t]
    #
    # We tile rows r, cols s, and reduction t to improve cache reuse and
    # exploit parallelism on a many-core CPU.
    #
    # TR, TS, TT, VEC_T, UNROLL_T are tunable constants; on a 32‑core x64
    # machine with AVX2, good starting points are:
    #   TR = TS ≈ 64, TT ≈ 64, VEC_T = 8, UNROLL_T = 2 or 4.

    # Tile the (r, s) output space into TR×TS tiles.
    block(r, R, TR)                 # outer tile index over rows of B
    block(s, S, TS)                 # outer tile index over cols of B

    # Tile the reduction dimension so that tiles of A[r, t] and A[s, t]
    # stay in cache while accumulating into B[r, s].
    block(t, T, TT)

    # Each (R, S) tile of B is independent: parallelize across tiles.
    parallelize(R)
    parallelize(S)

    # Within a tile, T iterates over contiguous t: vectorize and unroll
    # the reduction to exploit SIMD and ILP.
    vectorize(T, VEC_T)             # SIMD width in t (e.g., 4 or 8 elements)
    unroll(T, UNROLL_T)             # small unroll factor to hide latencies

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 3 (Cholesky_factor): left-looking in-place factorization
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The outer loops over i and j cannot be parallelized without changing
    # the algorithm, but the inner dot products over k are pure reductions.
    # We therefore optimize the k loops aggressively.

    # Vectorize the inner products acc_ij and acc_ii over k:
    #   acc += A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   acc += A[i, k] * A[i, k]
    # Using contiguous k gives efficient SIMD loads.
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)             # VEC_K ≈ SIMD width in elements

    # Partially unroll k to increase instruction-level parallelism while
    # keeping register pressure manageable.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)             # e.g., 2 or 4

    # Optionally block the outer i loop to improve temporal locality of
    # active rows when n is large. This preserves the sequential order in i.
    #
    # TI is a tunable block size (e.g., 32–64 rows).
    block(i, I, TI)

    # Hoist the tile index I to the outermost level to ensure that all
    # operations for an i-block are executed contiguously before moving
    # to the next block, improving cache behavior for A’s rows/columns.
    hoist(I)
```

```text
domain:
    # Global matrix size (from Polybench N). Treated as a parameter below.
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    r: dim in [0, N)
    s: dim in [0, N)
    t: dim in [0, N)        # reduction index for SPD initialization
    kc: dim in [0, N)       # reduction index for Cholesky factorization

data:
    # Main matrix A, modeled in row-major C layout: element A[i, j] == original C A[i][j].
    # In the Halide code this corresponds to Buffer access A(j, i).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Temporary matrix for SPD construction: B = A * A^T.
    # Same size and layout as A; lifetime limited to initialization.
    B[r, s]: temp DATA_TYPE = (r, s) -> r * N + s  # row-major

    # 1D temporary storing reciprocals of the diagonal after Cholesky steps:
    # Dinv[j] = 1 / A[j, j]. This lets us replace many divides with cheaper multiplies.
    Dinv[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j -> j               # contiguous 1D

parameters:
    N: int  # matrix dimension

    # Tuning parameters for SPD initialization (matrix-multiply-like phase).
    BR_init: int  # tile height in r
    BC_init: int  # tile width  in s
    BK_init: int  # tile size   in t
    V_init:  int  # SIMD width for s in SPD phase

    # Tuning parameters for Cholesky factorization.
    B_chol:  int  # block size for i (panel height)
    V_chol:  int  # SIMD width for kc in inner dot products
    U_chol:  int  # unroll factor for kc (small inner loops)

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (1) Build initial lower-triangular matrix L in A (diag = 1)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C reference:
    #   for i in 0..N-1:
    #     for j in 0..i:   A[i][j] = (-j % N) / N + 1
    #     for j in i+1..N-1: A[i][j] = 0
    #     A[i][i] = 1;
    INIT_LOWER:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, N):
                if j < i:
                    A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)(- (j mod N)) / (DATA_TYPE)(N) + (DATA_TYPE)(1)
                elif j == i:
                    A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)(1)
                else:
                    A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)(0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (2) Make matrix symmetric positive (semi-)definite: A := L * L^T
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Original C does:
    #   B[r][s] = 0;
    #   for t: for r: for s: B[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    #   A[r][s] = B[r][s];
    #
    # We exploit symmetry and only compute the lower triangle of B, then
    # mirror it to the upper triangle, halving the arithmetic.
    SPD_BUILD:
        for r in [0, N):
            for s in [0, r]:
                # B[r, s] = sum_t A[r, t] * A[s, t]
                B[r, s] = sum(t in [0, N), A[r, t] * A[s, t])
                # Symmetric fill of upper half:
                B[s, r] = B[r, s]

    SPD_COPY_BACK:
        for r in [0, N):
            for s in [0, N):
                A[r, s] = B[r, s]

    # After this phase, A is symmetric positive (semi-)definite.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (3) In-place Cholesky factorization: A -> L, with cached 1/diag
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reference algorithm (mapped to A[i, j]):
    #   for i in 0..N-1:
    #     for j in 0..i-1:
    #       A[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} A[i][k] * A[j][k]) / A[j][j];
    #     A[i][i] = sqrt(A[i][i] - sum_{k<i} A[i][k] * A[i][k]);
    #
    # Optimized variant:
    #   - Introduce Dinv[j] = 1 / A[j, j] after diagonal is computed.
    #   - Replace division in off-diagonal updates by multiplication:
    #       A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - sum_k A[i,k]*A[j,k]) * Dinv[j]
    #   This reduces O(N^2) divisions to O(N) divisions, keeping exact math
    #   modulo floating-point roundoff.
    CHOLESKY:
        for i in [0, N):

            # Off-diagonal elements in row i (0 <= j < i).
            for j in [0, i):
                A[i, j] =
                    (A[i, j] - sum(kc in [0, j), A[i, kc] * A[j, kc])) * Dinv[j]

            # Diagonal element at (i, i).
            A[i, i] =
                sqrt(A[i, i] - sum(kc in [0, i), A[i, kc] * A[i, kc]))

            # Cache reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
            Dinv[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(1) / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Initialization of L must finish before SPD_BUILD uses A.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        INIT_LOWER -> SPD_BUILD

    # SPD_BUILD and SPD_COPY_BACK must complete before Cholesky starts.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        SPD_COPY_BACK -> CHOLESKY

    # Within each row i of Cholesky:
    #  - Off-diagonal j loop is sequential because A[i, j] depends on
    #    previously computed A[i, kc] for kc < j.
    #  - Diagonal A[i, i] depends on all A[i, kc] with kc < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), j2 in [j+1, i):
        CHOLESKY(i, j) -> CHOLESKY(i, j2)   # j strictly increases

    # Each off-diagonal in column j for rows i > j depends on diagonal j
    # (via Dinv[j]).
    for j in [0, N), i in [j+1, N):
        CHOLESKY(j, j) -> CHOLESKY(i, j)

optimization:
    # ==============================
    # SPD initialization (B = A*A^T)
    # ==============================

    # Tile the SPD GEMM-like computation for better cache behavior.
    # r, s, t are blocked into outer tile indices Rb, Sb, Tb and inner
    # indices r, s, t (reused names).
    block(r, Rb, BR_init)    # r = Rb * BR_init + (inner r)
    block(s, Sb, BC_init)
    block(t, Tb, BK_init)

    # Hoist tile loops to outer levels to maximize reuse of A[r, t] and A[s, t]
    # across multiple B[r, s] elements.
    hoist(Rb)
    hoist(Sb)
    hoist(Tb)

    # Rows (or row tiles) of B are independent; safe to parallelize.
    parallelize(Rb)

    # Within each tile, vectorize over contiguous s for efficient SIMD loads.
    vectorize(s, V_init)

    # ==============================
    # Cholesky factorization
    # ==============================

    # Block the outer i-loop to operate on panels of rows. This improves
    # cache locality for the panel of columns 0..i and the corresponding
    # Dinv entries.
    block(i, I, B_chol)

    # Make the panel loop outermost so that work on each panel is done
    # before moving to the next, improving temporal locality.
    hoist(I)

    # Vectorize and unroll the inner reduction dimension kc (dot products)
    # inside both off-diagonal and diagonal updates.
    vectorize(kc, V_chol)
    unroll(kc, U_chol)

    # We intentionally do NOT parallelize i or j because of the strong
    # loop-carried dependencies in the Cholesky factorization (each row
    # depends on all previous rows and columns). Parallelism is exploited
    # only in the SPD initialization phase.
```

```text
domain:
    n: constant = N  # problem size

    # Indices for initialization of the lower-triangular seed matrix
    iL: dim in [0, n)
    jL: dim in [0, n)

    # Indices for SPD construction A = L0 * L0^T
    r: dim in [0, n)
    s: dim in [0, n)
    t: dim in [0, n)

    # Indices for Cholesky factorization
    iF: dim in [0, n)      # row being factorized; loop-carried dependency
    jF: dim in [0, n)      # column index below diagonal (jF < iF)
    kF: dim in [0, n)      # reduction index for off-diagonal dot product
    kDiag: dim in [0, n)   # reduction index for diagonal dot product

data:
    # Temporary lower-triangular seed matrix L0 used only during initialization.
    # Row-major layout: row index first, column index second.
    A_lower[iL, jL]: local DATA_TYPE = (iL, jL) -> iL * n + jL

    # Symmetric positive-definite matrix A, factored in place into its
    # Cholesky factor L (stored in the lower triangle of A).
    # Row-major layout for good locality when iterating over columns kF
    # with fixed row iF or jF.
    A[iF, jF]: inout DATA_TYPE = (iF, jF) -> iF * n + jF

parameters:
    n: int = N

    # Tuning parameters for SPD matrix construction (GEMM-like phase)
    Tr: int  # tile size in r (rows of A)
    Ts: int  # tile size in s (cols of A)
    Tt: int  # tile size in t (inner dimension)

    # Tuning parameters for Cholesky factorization
    Vk: int      # SIMD width for reductions over kF and kDiag
    UnrollK: int # unroll factor for reductions over kF, kDiag

computation:

    # 1. Build initial lower-triangular matrix L0 in A_lower.
    #
    # Equivalent to:
    #   for i in 0..n-1:
    #     for j in 0..i:   A[i][j] = (-(j % n))/n + 1
    #     for j in i+1..n-1: A[i][j] = 0
    #     A[i][i] = 1
    #
    init_lower:
        for iL in [0, n), jL in [0, n):
            A_lower[iL, jL] =
                if jL < iL  then (-(jL mod n)) / cast(DATA_TYPE, n) + cast(DATA_TYPE, 1)
                elif jL == iL then cast(DATA_TYPE, 1)
                else            cast(DATA_TYPE, 0)

    # 2. Form a symmetric positive-definite matrix A = L0 * L0^T.
    #
    # C-equivalent:
    #   for r in 0..n-1:
    #     for s in 0..n-1:
    #       A[r][s] = sum_{t=0}^{n-1} A_lower[r][t] * A_lower[s][t]
    #
    spd:
        for r in [0, n), s in [0, n):
            A[r, s] = sum(t in [0, n)) A_lower[r, t] * A_lower[s, t]

    # 3. In-place Cholesky factorization A = L L^T, storing L in the
    #    lower triangle of A. This matches the original Polybench kernel:
    #
    #   for i in 0..n-1:
    #     for j in 0..i-1:
    #       A[i][j] -= sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i][k] * A[j][k]
    #       A[i][j] /= A[j][j]
    #     A[i][i]  -= sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i][k] * A[i][k]
    #     A[i][i]   = sqrt(A[i][i])
    #
    chol:
        for iF in seq[0, n):  # must be strictly sequential
            # 3a. Off-diagonal elements in row iF, jF < iF.
            for jF in [0, iF):
                A[iF, jF] =
                    ( A[iF, jF]
                      - sum(kF in [0, jF)) A[iF, kF] * A[jF, kF] )
                    / A[jF, jF]

            # 3b. Diagonal element in row iF.
            A[iF, iF] =
                sqrt(
                    A[iF, iF]
                    - sum(kDiag in [0, iF)) A[iF, kDiag] * A[iF, kDiag]
                )

optimization:

    # --- SPD construction (matrix-matrix multiplication A = L0 * L0^T) ---

    # Tile the 3D loop nest (r, s, t) to improve cache reuse.
    # Each block (R, S) computes a Tr x Ts tile of A, accumulating
    # over the inner-dimension tiles of size Tt.
    block(r, R, Tr)        # r = R * Tr + r_in
    block(s, S, Ts)        # s = S * Ts + s_in
    block(t, T, Tt)        # t = T * Tt + t_in

    # Parallelize over row tiles of A; each thread handles a stripe of rows.
    # For sufficiently large n and enough cores, S can also be parallelized,
    # but avoiding nested parallelism simplifies scheduling.
    parallelize(R)

    # Use SIMD along the contiguous dimension of A (s, i.e. columns).
    # Choose vector width to match hardware SIMD lanes for DATA_TYPE.
    vectorize(s, 8)

    # Increase ILP in the accumulation over t by unrolling the inner tile.
    unroll(T, 4)

    # --- Cholesky factorization ---

    # The outer loop over iF must remain sequential, because row iF
    # depends on rows 0..iF-1. We therefore focus on making the inner
    # reductions efficient.

    # 1) SIMD and unrolling for reductions over kF (off-diagonal terms).
    #
    # Each update
    #   dot_ij = sum_{kF=0}^{jF-1} A[iF,kF] * A[jF,kF]
    # is a dot product. We can vectorize and unroll this inner loop.
    vectorize(kF, Vk)
    unroll(kF, UnrollK)

    # 2) SIMD and unrolling for reductions over kDiag (diagonal terms).
    #
    # Each update
    #   sum_ii = sum_{kDiag=0}^{iF-1} A[iF,kDiag]^2
    # is also a dot product and can be optimized similarly.
    vectorize(kDiag, Vk)
    unroll(kDiag, UnrollK)

    # 3) Hoist invariants out of the reduction loops.
    #
    # Values A[jF,jF] and the indices (iF, jF) are invariant w.r.t. kF
    # and kDiag; keep them in registers to reduce memory traffic.
    hoist(kF)
    hoist(kDiag)

    # 4) Optional parallel reductions over kF / kDiag.
    #
    # The reductions over kF and kDiag are associative sums of products.
    # They can be parallelized by computing partial sums in multiple
    # threads and combining them in a tree reduction; this changes only
    # the floating-point rounding, not the mathematical result.
    # This exposes parallelism even though iF itself is sequential.
    #
    # Note: requires a reduction-aware implementation (e.g., rfactor-style
    # transformation) to introduce private accumulators per worker.
    #parallelize(kF)
    #parallelize(kDiag)

    # 5) Cache-friendly blocking over iF (optional).
    #
    # For large n and large last-level caches, further improve locality
    # by working on panels of rows of height Ti that fit into cache:
    #
    #   block(iF, IF, Ti)
    #   hoist(IF)                   # process panels outermost
    #
    # Within each panel, the schedule above for kF/kDiag remains.
    # Any additional workspaces used for such panel blocking should be
    # sized O(n * Ti) with Ti <= n/2, ensuring extra memory usage
    # remains below 50% of the main n x n matrix A.
```

```text
# Optimized model for in-place Cholesky factorization (timed kernel)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)    # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)    # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)    # reduction index for dot products

data:
    # Symmetric positive-definite matrix; only the lower triangle (j <= i) is
    # read and written by the factorization. Upper triangle is ignored.
    #
    # Layout matches the effective C layout A[i][j] used in the original code:
    # A(i, j) == A[i][j], contiguous in j for fixed i (row-major).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major 2D array

parameters:
    N: int                         # matrix dimension
    TI: int                        # tile size along i (e.g. 32 or 64)
    TK: int                        # tile size for the k reduction (e.g. 64 or 128)
    VK: int                        # SIMD width for k (e.g. 8 for float on AVX2, 16 on AVX-512)

computation:
    # Precondition (not modeled here): A is initialized to an N×N
    # symmetric positive-definite matrix, e.g. as in init_array(), before timing.
    #
    # Goal: overwrite A with a lower-triangular factor L such that
    #       original_A = L * L^T.
    # Only entries A[i, j] with j <= i are used and defined at the end.

    # 1. Off-diagonal elements: i > j
    #    A[i, j] := (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0..j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]) / A[j, j]
    #
    # This is a left-looking update: for fixed (i, j), we dot-product
    # the prefixes of rows i and j up to length j, then scale by 1 / A[j, j].
    #
    cholesky_offdiag:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # j must be processed strictly in increasing order because
            # A[i, j] depends on A[i, k] with k < j, which are updated
            # earlier in the same i-iteration.
            for j in seq([0, i)):
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j): A[i, k] * A[j, k] )
                    ) / A[j, j]

    # 2. Diagonal elements: i == j
    #    A[i, i] := sqrt(A[i, i] - sum_{k=0..i-1} A[i, k] * A[i, k])
    #
    # This uses the fully-updated off-diagonal entries in row i.
    #
    cholesky_diag:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            A[i, i] =
                sqrt( A[i, i]
                      - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[i, k] ) )

dependencies:
    # For each fixed row i, off-diagonal entries must be computed left-to-right in j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i-1]:
        cholesky_offdiag(i, j) -> cholesky_offdiag(i, j + 1)

    # Diagonal update for row i depends on all off-diagonal updates in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            cholesky_offdiag(i, j) -> cholesky_diag(i)

optimization:
    # The algorithm is fundamentally sequential in i (and in j for each i),
    # so we *do not* parallelize across i or j. We instead:
    #   - tile i to improve cache reuse,
    #   - tile and vectorize the reduction dimension k to exploit SIMD,
    #   - mildly unroll k for ILP.
    #
    # These do not change the mathematical result; they only change loop
    # structure and evaluation order inside the associative sums.

    # 1. Panel/blocking in the outer i dimension.
    #
    # Process the matrix in vertical panels of height TI, so nearby rows
    # share cache-resident prefixes A[i, 0..k] and A[j, 0..k] while we run
    # many dot products.
    #
    # Conceptually transforms:
    #   for i in [0, N):
    #       ...
    # into:
    #   for I in [0, ceil(N / TI)):
    #       for i in [I*TI, min((I+1)*TI, N)):
    #           ...
    #
    block(i, I, TI)
    hoist(I)   # make panel loop I the outermost loop for both stages

    # 2. Block the reduction dimension k to improve temporal locality and
    #    expose a clean inner vectorized loop.
    #
    # The reductions:
    #   sum(k in [0, j)) A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[i, k]
    # are split into tiles of size TK; each tile operates on a contiguous
    # slice of both rows involved, which maps well to caches and SIMD.
    #
    # Conceptually:
    #   sum(k in [0, L)) ...  =>
    #     sum(K in [0, ceil(L / TK)) {
    #         sum(k in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, L))) ...
    #     }
    #
    block(k, K, TK)

    # 3. Vectorize the inner k-loop inside each tile K.
    #
    # Within a tile, the loop over k becomes the innermost loop and
    # operates on contiguous elements of A[i, k] and A[j, k], so it maps
    # directly to SIMD vector instructions (e.g., AVX2/AVX-512).
    #
    # Since we express the k-loop as a mathematical sum(), the order of
    # accumulation within a tile can be safely changed for performance
    # (up to usual floating-point roundoff differences).
    #
    vectorize(K, VK)

    # 4. Light unrolling inside the vectorized k-tile to improve ILP and
    #    hide instruction latencies without blowing up code size.
    #
    # This can be implemented as unrolling the scalar "remainder" loop
    # and/or unrolling the vector loop by a small factor, e.g. 4.
    #
    unroll(K, 4)

    # Note: we intentionally avoid parallelize(I) or parallelize(i/j) because
    # of strong loop-carried dependencies in Cholesky. Parallelism, if
    # desired, should instead target higher-level blocked Cholesky variants
    # or the SPD initialization phase, not this strictly left-looking core.
```
